exactGap: A Cmd/Ctrl+K and bare '/' overlay already exists (CoreNavbar.tsx:122-132, 463), but it is a knowledge search over Data Plane retrieval plus a client-side title filter over local chat history, not web search; its results are plain buttons with no focus trap, arrow keys or Enter handling (UI_UX_AUDIT:71, no ArrowDown handler in CoreNavbar.tsx). There is no command registry, Space/room/agent quick switcher, shortcut sheet, number-key room switching or platform slash commands: the Space composer's '/' opens a skill picker only (SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:272). The 'To:' picker has nothing to find because the gateway accepts only personal|room Spaces (spaces.rs:2873), so no DM or group-DM kind and no people directory exist.
reuse: CoreNavbar search overlay shell (open/close, Escape, debounce, searchNavbar) as the palette container; fold the knowledge and local-chat-history groups in as providers

ActionDescriptor registry (id, label, description, risk, requiresApproval, zod inputSchema; 14 spaces.* actions) as the action source, executed only through ActionCommand preview then execute and the gateway dispatcher
SpaceRoomComposer listbox picker (role=listbox, aria-activedescendant, arrow/Enter/Tab/Escape) as the keyboard-model reference
DashboardComposer BUILTIN_COMMANDS and matchDraftCommand shape (name, aliases, description, builtin) as the only existing slash-command catalogue
listSpaces, getSpaceThreads, getSpaceRoster, getAgentInstallations clients and space-live-work.ts live/unread store as palette sources
constraints: Phase 1 is Frontend-only and safe: every source is an existing Control-gated gateway read, so the palette cannot widen what a viewer already sees. Actions must go through ActionCommand/the gateway dispatcher so audit and approval stay with the owning plane, and requiresApproval actions never run directly from the palette. model-eligibility.ts is a separate execution-claim allowlist (empty by default), so 'human-eligible' is simply every registry entry; filter by risk/requiresApproval instead, and note most spaces.* actions need arguments (spaceRef, memberId) that a palette must prompt for. Recent-item history in the palette must obey isLocalRetentionAllowed (ZDR). Thread search is limited to titles/previews already fetched; message search does not exist (F-t1-018). The 'To:' phase is blocked until a DM/group kind and people directory exist in Control/Application.
approachAdjustment: Correct the premise: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens knowledge search plus local chat history, not web search (web search lives in the Home search panel); keep both groups as palette providers instead of 'moving web search'. Ship the switcher (rooms, threads of loaded rooms, agents, roster people) and the missing keyboard model first. ActionDescriptor has no hotkey or when field, so add them in a thin command wrapper rather than mutating the registry; execute registry actions only where input is derivable (mark_read, set_agent_state for the current room) or after a schema-driven argument prompt. Split the 'To:' picker into its own blocked item behind DMs.
effortNote: Unchanged for phases 1-2 (palette, switcher, keyboard model, shortcut sheet, a few platform slash commands). The To: picker is a separate XL that is blocked on a DM kind and directory, and arg-prompting for registry actions adds work if included.
verdictReason: The gap is real (no palette, switcher, shortcut sheet or platform commands) but the item misdescribes what Cmd/Ctrl+K opens today and bundles a To: picker that cannot be built yet.

exactGap: No call, huddle or live screen-share code exists in Spaces or anywhere under apps/ (git grep finds no RTCPeerConnection, SFU, livekit or mediasoup use; getDisplayMedia appears once, as a one-frame screenshot capture in DashboardComposer.tsx:1915-1950), so this item cannot start before the call stack it depends on (F-t1-029), which is also absent. The agent-acting cue is only partly present as an 'is working...' row per post and a composer line (SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:349-366, SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:176-182, 617-630); there is no Space browser view, the FleetRunConsole live-view cells are placeholder text (FleetRunConsole.tsx:116-131), and the real hosted-browser view with human_takeover lives only on Home/chat (BrowserChrome.tsx:497). The Space definition lists huddles as an explicit non-goal (space-defenition.md:352-353).
reuse: DashboardComposer.addScreenshotFile getDisplayMedia handling (stop all tracks, cancel is a no-op) as the capture starting point
Space working row and composer line plus space-live-work.ts live-run projection as the agent-acting cue that already exists in text form
BrowserChrome controlMode/human_takeover chip and approval bubble as the design source for an agent-acting border once a Space browser view exists
SpaceApprovalPanel as the surface to mask in a redacted-while-sharing mode
packages/remote-core (RustDesk WebSocket client used by RemoteSupportPage) is a separate remote-desktop path and not a base for an SFU share
constraints: No plane owns a media/SFU service today, so human screen share is not a Frontend-only change: a call needs a media service (Application Plane realtime or Infra) with join authorization from a Control Space-membership decision, and ZDR requires that no recording, transcript or content is retained. The agent-acting cue must be rendered from Model Plane run state and, for browsers, Quarry session state; the Frontend only displays it (Model proposes, Quarry executes), and a Space-scoped agent browser view does not exist yet. A web page cannot exclude its own windows from capture, so in-app redaction is best-effort and must not be advertised as a guarantee. Calls/huddles conflict with the documented Space non-goal, so this needs a product decision.
approachAdjustment: Split the item. Keep the agent-acting cue as its own small item built on the existing run-status projection (S, Frontend only, extends the 'is working' row with the current tool or browser step). Move human screen share behind an explicit call decision as an optional later item and drop the claim that it is cheap, since the SFU and signalling do not exist. If it is ever built, scope the first cut to share-a-tab with a sharing bar and a warning, and treat redaction of approval cards as a UI nicety rather than a safeguard.
effortNote: M holds only for the incremental share track after a call stack exists; none exists, and an SFU plus authorization and signalling is an XL by itself. The agent-cue half alone is S.
verdictReason: Absent, hard-dependent on a call stack that also does not exist, and contrary to the documented Space non-goal on huddles; only the agent-acting cue half deserves to stay as a small separate item.

exactGap: The Space composer is a two-row plain textarea that is disabled while a turn streams and is cleared before the send starts, so a failed send loses the draft; it keeps no drafts, attachments, paste chips, human scheduled send or context chips (SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:147, 387, 745-746), and human posts render as plain text while agent posts use ChatMarkdown (SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:329-336). The queue/steer backend is already Space-aware (gateway chat.rs:40-44 and json_handlers.rs:176-205 mint a fresh content-bound Control append decision; use-chat-controller.ts:2208-2223 passes spaceRef), but SpaceRoomComposer imports only streamChat and cancelInvocation (line 4). Home already has the pieces to extract (ZDR-gated draft hook, paste-to-attachment chips, attachment preparation, mid-run submit), no client idempotency key is sent (none in chat-client.ts; spaces.rs:137 generates one when absent), and chat document upload is user-scoped, not Space-bound (documents.rs:54).
reuse: useHomeDraft and home-draft-storage (sessionStorage, 400 ms debounce, ZDR gate via isLocalRetentionAllowed, identity-keyed) for Space drafts keyed by user, org, space and thread
DashboardComposer paste-to-attachment helpers (4000-char threshold, pastedTextAttachmentFile) and prepareChatAttachments, extracted into a shared module
queueInvocationInput client plus the gateway queue route, which already takes space_ref and re-mints a Control thread:append decision
ChatMarkdown for human posts (after the link rules in F-t1-030 land)
Model Plane moderation scan_injection and trust-class framing for untrusted context blocks
capability-core cron_schedules (Space-scoped, re-authorized per fire) for any later scheduled send
constraints: Every Space send needs a fresh Control thread:append decision bound to the exact bytes (spaces.rs inject_personal_thread_context), so drafts, queued chips and any scheduled send must re-obtain a decision at send time. All posts currently go through the chat/model stream and the Space router has no human-only post route (INF: every send is a model invocation), so a scheduled human post needs the category 01 human-only path first. Attachments must become Data Plane documents bound to the Space with a Control grant and must never widen an owner-plane ACL; today's chat document upload is user-scoped, and ZDR attachments must not reach external services. Drafts in browser storage must be cleared under ZDR (reuse the retention gate). The schedule primitive is owned by Model Plane capability-core cron_schedules, not Control. Steer by a non-owner needs the shared-append authority (F-t1-001). Context chips must pass refs, with the Model Plane framing them as quoted untrusted data and screenshots dropped under ZDR.
approachAdjustment: Drop the Tiptap/ProseMirror editor: a markdown textarea with a small toolbar and live preview gives most of the value without the bundle and Solid integration risk, so demote the rich-text editor. Reuse the existing ZDR-aware useHomeDraft instead of building revision tombstones (sessionStorage is tab-local, so the cross-tab resurrection race the tombstones solve does not arise). Wire queueInvocationInput into SpaceRoomComposer (backend already Space-aware) and restore the draft on a failed send, render human posts through ChatMarkdown, and extract the Home composer's paste chips and attachment preparation rather than rewriting them. Correct the owner of scheduled send to Model Plane capability-core and defer it. Split the context-chip 'Ask the agent about this' work into its own item that follows the canvas, file and artifact surfaces.
effortNote: As one bundle it is closer to XL. Split: drafts, failed-send restore and human markdown rendering are S; queue/steer wiring is M; attachments and paste chips need a new Space-bound upload path (L); scheduled send and context chips are separate L items; the rich-text editor is demoted.
verdictReason: The composer gaps are real and the Space-aware queue backend and ZDR draft hook make the first slices cheap, but the item bundles six features, overbuilds the editor and drafts, and mis-assigns the schedule primitive.

The Sparkles/initials avatar split in SpaceRoomTimeline as the human-versus-agent baseline to extend
constraints: Avatar colour is presentation only and must never enter an authority decision (schema.ts:328-329 says so); the BFF already validates it as a six-digit hex, so the same validator should guard the new read path. The hover card may show an approval state, but a run belongs to the member who started it and only that member can decide (SpaceApprovalPanel.tsx header), so the card must not expose approval details or controls to other members beyond 'waiting on <owner>'. Agent identity comes from an Application binding joined to a Control roster entry; an agent Control authorizes but Application has not described must keep rendering as 'identity not published' with a neutral avatar, never an invented colour. exactGap: Nothing for out-of-tab attention exists in the SPA: index.html links only an icon and the static title 'verevonv3', public/ has no manifest or service worker, and a source search finds no service worker, Notification/Push API, setAppBadge or dynamic document.title outside the demo guard, so the only cues are in-tab navbar unread counts and sidebar unread dots (CoreNavbar.tsx:86-90, CoreSidebarSpacesPanel.tsx:288-317). notification-core has no web-push path: 'push' is Novu vocabulary behind a disabled-by-default adapter (runtime/client.go:48, 105, 201-219), every ZDR delivery is marked failed (delivery_worker.go:92), and its consumers cover only inbox, mail-task, social, session and org-deletion events, none for Space posts, agent-run completion or approvals. The delivery ledger the item depends on (S4.4) is unbuilt: the Watch primitive deliberately stops at 'recorded' (capability-core watch.go:6-9).
evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/public (directory listing: no manifest or service worker)
apps/Application Plane/notification-core/internal/consumers (file list: control_session, conversation_followed_message, mail_task_drafted, social_publish_failed, org_deletion)
reuse: space-live-work.ts unread and live-thread maps plus the Convex spaceReadMarkers and mark_space_read route as the single unread projection for title, favicon and app badge
notification-core feed, preferences, subscribers and delivery-worker framework (recipient resolver, retention check) as the home for push subscriptions
capability-core Watch primitive and the future S4.4 delivery ledger as the source of agent-finished and needs-approval events
SpaceApprovalPanel and the Space #chat deep link (activity-grammar.ts:199) as the Open target; approvals are never decided from a toast
nginx.conf per-extension locations as the pattern for a dedicated no-cache /sw.js and manifest location
constraints: Subscription storage and fan-out belong to Application Plane notification-core, not the Frontend; the wake payload must be an opaque id with no content, and delivery_worker.go currently refuses every ZDR request, so the content-free wake needs an explicit carve-out decided by Control retention policy rather than a blanket lift. Producing the events is Model Plane (run completion, approval requested) and Control (membership), so the item depends on notification-core gaining Space/run/approval consumers that do not exist. Whatever the service worker renders must be authorized for the recipient at read time (the existing recipientResolver pattern) and must not widen Space access; approvals stay with the run owner. nginx.conf:103 gives every .js file a one-year immutable header, so /sw.js needs its own no-cache location, and stale-worker pinning needs build-keyed invalidation. Space definition lists notification polish as a non-goal, so keep scope to agent attention. Any third-party push provider needs ZDR proof even for a constant payload.
approachAdjustment: Slice it. Slice A (S, Frontend only): tab title with an unread count, favicon dot, navigator.setAppBadge and an in-tab toast, all fed from the existing space-live-work unread/live projection and honoring per-room mute. Slice B (M): manifest, icons, install affordance and a minimal service worker that caches only the shell, with its own nginx location. Slice C (L): Web Push, which first needs notification-core producers for Space, run and approval events and the S4.4 delivery ledger. The scoped short-lived token for the service worker is probably unnecessary because a same-origin service-worker fetch carries the session cookie (INF, needs a quick test); an expired session can simply render a generic 'Open Verevon' notification. The browser permission prompt should come from an explicit setting, not on load.
effortNote: As written (PWA plus Web Push plus toasts plus badge, with five dependencies) it is more than L; sliced, A is S, B is M and C is L, and C is blocked on notification-core event producers and the delivery ledger.
verdictReason: The need is real and nothing exists, but the status is absent rather than partial, the item is three slices of very different size, and push cannot start until notification-core has Space-event producers and a ZDR-safe wake class.

exactGap: The server side is already deny-by-default: room transcript, thread list, activity, knowledge and work reads all take a Control shared-read decision and the transcript route returns 403 space_read_not_authorized (spaces.rs:2616-2680), but SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:201 swallows that 403 with .catch(() => null) and falls back to the thread preview, and a declined read leaves the thread list owner-bound (spaces.rs:1158-1165), so a room whose org has not enabled shared reads silently shows only your own posts as previews. nginx.conf:70 enforces a CSP with connect-src 'self' https:, img-src 'self' data: https: blob: and style-src 'unsafe-inline' and has no Trusted Types, report-only policy or report endpoint, and the markdown renderer builds [text](url) anchors with no scheme or destination check (chat-media-markdown.tsx:1278-1279), though script-src 'self' without unsafe-inline already blocks javascript: execution. Spaces have no attachments or download route to protect (chat documents upload is user-scoped, documents.rs:54), so a per-room attachment ACL is moot until attachments ship.
reuse: The existing Control shared-read decision on every Space read route (shared_thread_read_decision) as the single authorization point; add attachments to it rather than a parallel check
sandbox-html.ts preview CSP plus sandbox="allow-scripts" without allow-same-origin for any agent HTML
Mermaid securityLevel strict and KaTeX trust false, which already close the few innerHTML sinks (only three exist in src)
nginx.conf CSP variable and its per-location re-emit pattern for adding a Report-Only header
Gateway nosniff header (main.rs:157) for download responses
constraints: Authorization stays with Control and the owning plane through the gateway; the restricted state is a UI rendering of the existing 403 and must not leak anything the read decision withheld (the preview fallback is only safe because the declined listing is owner-bound). The 403 is a per-room or per-org policy outcome, not a per-post one, so it is one room-level message. Tightening connect-src and img-src is a Frontend Plane nginx change, but connect-src https: is deliberately broad for Nexi and telemetry and img-src https: serves web-search thumbnails, favicons and remote chat media (nginx.conf:46-70, DashboardSearchResults.tsx), so narrowing needs a host inventory and a media proxy and must roll out Report-Only first. Third-party Turnstile and Nexi scripts can break under Trusted Types. Attachment read checks belong to the future Space attachment contract (Data Plane document with a Space-bound grant), not to this item.
approachAdjustment: Re-scope to what is real. (1) S: render a room-level 'restricted' state when the transcript or thread read is refused, instead of silently showing previews. (2) S: add a scheme allowlist (https and mailto) and show the destination host for external markdown links, which also covers link-text spoofing; javascript: is already blocked by script-src but defense in depth is cheap, and the more important need grows once human posts render through ChatMarkdown (F-t1-032). (3) M: a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only candidate with a gateway report endpoint, then narrow connect-src and img-src behind a media proxy. Demote Trusted Types (three innerHTML sinks, all already sanitized, and DOMPurify is not a direct dependency) and drop SRI (script-src is 'self' on same-origin hashed assets, so SRI adds little). Remove the standalone attachment-ACL work and attach it to the attachments feature.
effortNote: Unchanged in size but re-scoped: restricted state and link rules are S, the CSP report-only rollout is the M part; Trusted Types and SRI are removed or demoted.
verdictReason: The deny-by-default server gate and the sandboxed agent-HTML path already exist, so the item should shrink to the swallowed 403, link safety and a report-only CSP rollout, and drop the attachment-ACL, Trusted Types and SRI work.

exactGap: No search over Space messages, threads, runs, approvals or artifacts exists: gateway search routes cover only web, similar, suggest, images, videos and answer (search.rs:39-45), the Cmd/Ctrl+K overlay is knowledge retrieval plus a client-side title filter over local chat history (navbar.rs:262-283, CoreNavbar.tsx:403-409), and the Space Knowledge tab is a read-only list with no search box (SpaceKnowledgePanel.tsx:82-110). Session Core has no search RPC, and the retrieval engine strips ':' field selectors from queries (textquery.rs:127), so an operator grammar has nothing to compile to until a Session Core message search (F-t1-018) exists. The one existing pattern to copy is the ZDR-gated, identity-keyed browser history for web searches (web-history.ts:1-40).
evidence: buzz: desktop/src/features/search/lib/parseSearchOperators.test.mjs (parser to port; confirmed present via git grep)

The Space activity route (GET /spaces/:ref/activity) which already composes threads, runs, approvals, receipts and grants, so run and approval tabs can start as a filter over that per-room projection
web-history.ts pattern (ZDR gate via chat-retention, identity-keyed storage, URL validation) for recent searches
The F-t1-018 search UI shell and the CoreNavbar overlay
constraints: Message search must be a Session Core (Model Plane) read under the same Control shared-read decision and audience filtering as the transcript; the gateway may fan out and compose but must not join across planes, and each backend needs its own Control decision. Name-to-id resolution for from: must come from the Space roster the viewer is already allowed to read. ZDR threads are temporary and must stay unsearchable, and recent-search history must stay browser-local and obey isLocalRetentionAllowed. Do not forward operator text to retrieval-engine/Quickwit, which strips ':' syntax; parse in the client or gateway and send structured filters.
approachAdjustment: Sequence it behind F-t1-018. The operator parser is an S module that can land with the search UI, mapping to a structured filter {authors, spaces, since, until, is, has, agent}. Typed tabs for runs, approvals and artifacts should first be a client-side filter over the per-room activity projection (no new owner-plane endpoint), with cross-room fan-out only later; the item's 'owner-plane search endpoints not confirmed to exist' dependency is true for Session Core messages but not for per-room runs and approvals. Share the filter struct with the agent history tool (F-t1-038) as proposed.
effortNote: Unchanged for this item alone; it excludes the Session Core message search (F-t1-018), which is a separate M to L Model Plane build and the real critical path.
verdictReason: Nothing exists and the item is blocked on message search that does not exist; operators are a refinement of search, not a first-order Space need, so it should follow F-t1-018 rather than lead.

exactGap: Activity rows already emit /spaces/{id}?thread_id=...#chat (activity-grammar.ts:199-200), but only the hash tab is read (SpaceCockpit.tsx:120-125, 139-162) and App.tsx registers just /spaces/:spaceId (181-182), so the link lands on the room and nothing scrolls or highlights. Pin is a Session Core thread flag that only the post's author can set (spaces.rs:2183-2310 returns thread_presentation_owner_only; SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:229-257) and the timeline sorts purely by time (137-141), so pins are flagged, not lifted; reply continues a thread rather than quoting an entry (SpacePage.tsx:519-533), and there is no fork or forward (session-core has no fork RPC; sessions.proto:250-262 only anticipates replay, share and fork). The prerequisites exist: every message carries a durable message_id and its Space audience snapshot (sessions.proto:942, migration 0025, grpc.rs:2571-2580) but the Space client drops the id (spaces-client.ts:606-660).
reuse: chat-thread-deep-link.ts validated reader and builder (fail-closed, length and control-character checks) as the model for a Space entry link module
Session Core per-message message_id, sequence and the inherited Space audience snapshot (migration 0025) as the entry reference and as the fork prerequisite
The existing shared-read decision plus audience-revision binding on thread creation (sessions.proto:250-262) for resolving an entry under the viewer audience
SpaceCockpit hash-tab handling and SpaceRoomPost unread flags for scroll-to and highlight
The Convex Space projections (spaceReadMarkers, spaceMembers) as the pattern for a room pins table owned by Application Plane
constraints: Entry references must be resolved server-side under the viewer's audience revision and must reveal no title or preview to non-members (do not store denormalized quote text). Room pins by Space role are a Space-level curation fact: store them in Application Plane next to spaceReadMarkers with a Control role decision (editor and above), and keep reading the pinned content through Session Core under the viewer's own decision; thread presentation is today written only by Session Core and owner-bound, so do not loosen that rule in place. An agent pin tool is a model-initiated action and must first earn a model-eligibility.ts entry (owner contract, forged-call denial). Fork belongs to Session Core, copies only rows the forking viewer can see (or the intersection across members), and must be denied for ZDR threads (QM plan verification list). Forward needs a fresh Control decision for the destination Space and must not carry source retrieval grants. Notification payloads should carry entity refs rather than hrefs.
approachAdjustment: Slice by cost. First, make the existing links work: SpacePage reads thread_id (validated like readThreadDeepLink), scrolls to that post and highlights it (S, Frontend only, and the thread is already the room's post unit). Second, pass Session Core's message_id through the Space transcript client so entries inside a thread are addressable, adding /spaces/:id/m/:entry (S to M). Third, Space-role pins in an Application Plane table with timeline lifting (M). Then fork as a Session Core RPC (L; per-message audience snapshots already exist) and quote with a server-resolved tombstone (M). Demote forward, which is the riskiest for the authority model. Correct the item's citation: grpc.rs:5340-5360 is the agent-skills listing, not audience filtering; cite sessions.proto:250-262 and migration 0025 instead.
effortNote: Unchanged overall but should be split: deep-link fix S, entry permalinks S to M, Space-role pins M, fork L, quote M, forward demoted.
verdictReason: The gaps are confirmed and already tracked, but several slices are far cheaper than the item implies (links already emitted, message_id already exposed by Session Core, audience columns already on messages), so the item should be sliced and forward demoted.
